name: DeepSeek Harness
summary: Plugin-based open-source agent framework from DeepSeek AI ("everything is a plugin") built on the Cordis composable plugin system, with a web UI and CLI for building and running custom agents.

agent-runtime.note: Core agent loop and web UI for agent interaction.

orchestration.note: No built-in DAG/workflow engine; composition is expressed through the plugin architecture.

knowledge-memory.note: No built-in document store, embeddings, or memory — provided by plugins.

tools-integration.note: The plugin system is the tool/extension surface; capabilities are added as Cordis plugins.

identity-governance.note: No multi-tenant IAM, policies, quotas, approvals, or audit log.

observability.note: Run visibility through the web UI; no structured trace/usage/audit model.

data-secrets.note: No managed file storage or encrypted secrets store.

evaluation.note: No built-in datasets, scorers, or eval runs.

channels.note: Web UI is built in; messaging-platform gateways arrive as Cordis plugins.

code-execution.note: No first-party sandbox; execution environments are provided by plugins.

human-in-loop.note: An approval package supplies a fail-closed approval service that gates each tool call under a per-session ask or never policy, plus a seam for free-form questions to the user.

multi-tenancy.note: Workspaces are local user directories holding session membership, and the identity package states its values do not represent an authenticated account, so no tenant-scoped permission model exists.

declarative-deployment.note: An agent preset declaratively composes a session's tools, persona, and prompt sections, but it is per-session composition with no plan/apply, dependency graph, or resource provisioning.

agent-versioning.note: No versioned agent definitions, aliases, canary rollout, or rollback appear in the packages or subsystem documentation.

skill-learning.note: The skill family only discovers pre-authored skills through filesystem providers and exposes a read-only catalog and loader; there is no write path for the agent to author a skill.
